Implement and verify in GLLA on main, then release the next patch including the existing unreleased paragraph and audit fixes and verify publication. Use the supplied GLLA, Deathrun, Neonbreak, drafting, and recovery screenshots as regression examples; do not merely truncate useful explanations or hide failed/skipped checks. Preserve full archival evidence, truthful verdicts, confirmation/ownership gates, lifecycle barriers, and archive-before-success. Implement and verify in GLLA on main, then release the next patch including the existing unreleased paragraph and audit fixes and verify publication. Exclude note.md Later/Research, unrelated improvements, modifications to Pi core or other plugins/projects, and new speculative queue work. If a reported symptom is external-only, document the evidence and provide only safe GLLA-owned containment rather than expanding scope.

goal.objective: Improve GLLA's drafting-to-completion experience across all five remaining concerns: (1) use ask_user_question for structured drafting decisions when available, retaining prose for genuinely free-form questions or tool unavailability; (2) organize drafting into visible phases, batching independent questions and asking dependent questions after earlier answers; (3) diagnose and fix GLLA-owned unfinished drafting handoffs so a draft does not silently end after promising more questions, while preserving intentional waits for user input and preventing retry loops; (4) distinguish deliberate user pauses from supervised recovery/retry and actual monitoring, exposing truthful ownership and next action without claiming monitoring that does not exist; (5) make terminal summaries explain what changed and why it matters first, in readable groups, with compact verification and explicit limitations, moving detailed commands, hashes, and repository bookkeeping into the durable archive. Fix broken evidence-stripping fragments, duplicated approval/process text, oversized narrative tables, and loss of the whole-work recap after an audit-repair claim. Preserve full archival evidence, truthful verdicts, confirmation/ownership gates, lifecycle barriers, and archive-before-success. Implement and verify in GLLA on main, then release the next patch including the existing unreleased paragraph and audit fixes and verify publication. Exclude note.md Later/Research, unrelated improvements, modifications to Pi core or other plugins/projects, and new speculative queue work. If a reported symptom is external-only, document the evidence and provide only safe GLLA-owned containment rather than expanding scope.

I’ll include that evidence in the audit report. I won’t edit the code or tests while acting as the independent auditor.
The proposed bug is already reproduced through `buildStatusText`. The drafting questionnaire does not trigger that classification path, and editing a test or the implementation would violate this read-only audit’s constraints. I’ll finish with the required fixes.
The hypothesis does not apply to this independent audit: two blocking behaviors are now reproduced, so further implementation work belongs to the executor. I’m collecting the final verification excerpts and returning the verdict.

- Screenshot-shaped evidence references still leave **`(,2760)`** in the terminal explanation.

The saved completion fixture is cleaner but too generic to establish preservation of the supplied examples’ substantive explanations. `note.md` also still says release verification is pending.
